business.title: Volume of retail trade down by 0.6% in the euro area and by 0.4% in the EU
business.description: Overview In July 2026, compared with June 2026, the seasonally adjusted retail trade volume decreased by 0.6% in the euro area and by 0.4% in the EU, according to first estimates from Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union. In June 2026, retail trade volume grew by 0.2% in both the euro area and the EU. In July 2026, compared with July 2025, the calendar adjusted retail sales index increased by 0.6% in the euro area and by 1.0% in the EU. Monthly comparison by retail sector and by Member State In the euro area in July 2026, compared with June 2026, the volume of retail trade increased for food, drinks, tobacco by 0.4%, decreased for non-food products (except automotive fuel) by 1.4%, decreased for automotive fuel in specialised stores by 0.8%. In the EU, the volume of retail trade increased for food, drinks, tobacco by 0.3%, decreased for non-food products (except automotive fuel) by 1.1%, decreased for automotive fuel in specialised stores by 1.1%. Among Member States for which data are available, the largest monthly decreases in the total retail trade volume were recorded in Germany (-3.4%), Spain (-0.9%), Italy and Poland (both -0.3%). The highest increases were observed in Latvia (+2.5%), Cyprus (+2.0%) and Luxembourg (+1.8%). Annual comparison by retail sector and by Member State In the euro area in July 2026, compared with July 2025, the volume of retail trade increased for food, drinks, tobacco by 1.6%, increased for non-food products (except automotive fuel) by 0.2%, decreased for automotive fuel in specialised stores by 3.1%. In the EU, the volume of retail trade increased for food, drinks, tobacco by 1.3%, increased for non-food products (except automotive fuel) by 0.9%, decreased for automotive fuel in specialised stores by 2.0%. Among Member States for which data are available, the highest annual increases in the total retail trade volume were recorded in Cyprus (+8.6%), Latvia (+7.1%) and Sweden (+6.4%). Decreases were observed in Romania (-5.7%), Germany (-2.5%), Italy (-1.0%) and Spain (-0.7%). science.description: Stargazers at Brandon University are eager to try out the new dome that protects their state-of-the-art telescope at the top of McMaster Hall - the telescope that is the largest publicly accessible telescope in Canada between Thunder Bay and Calgary. The original dome was built to protect the original telescope when McMaster Hall was constructed in 1971. In 2009 the telescope was replaced with the current Ritchey-Chretien telescope that features a 16-inch diameter, just a bit larger than the comparable telescope at the University of Manitoba. And while the telescope itself had been replaced, the 1971 protective dome remained in service for decades. Due to its age and weather-related deterioration, the dome needed to be replaced to further protect the telescope.
